new_statements.quote: L'otomi est-il une langue à tons ? Pour Ecker, l'otomi n'est pas à proprement parler une langue à tons. Mais divers auteurs sont en désaccord sur ce point, car certains traits prosodiques tels que les faits d'accentuation jouent un rôle déterminant. L'existence de tons paraît aujourd'hui démontrée. Exemple : (3e personne Futur tà mpa : il s'en va), (1ère " Passé tá mpa : je suis parti). On remarquera que, dans certains parlers, cette opposition tonale est évitée par des changements phonématiques. [...] Les phénomènes d'intonation tiennent une place très importante et permettent de distinguer un sous-dialecte d'un autre
new_statements.translation: Is Otomi a tone language? For Ecker, Otomi is not strictly speaking a tone language. But various authors disagree, since certain prosodic features such as accentuation play a determining role. The existence of tones now appears demonstrated. Example: (3rd person future tà mpa 'he goes away'), (1st person past tá mpa 'I left'). Note that in some local varieties this tonal opposition is avoided by segmental changes. [...] Intonation phenomena are very important and allow one sub-dialect to be distinguished from another.

México: Mission Archéologique et Ethnologique Française au Mexique. OpenEdition Books re-edition (CEMCA), Introduction, section 'Mode de transcription phonologique et problèmes du bilinguisme' (paras 36-71). [Spanish ed.: Pueblos de la Sierra Madre: etnografía de la comunidad otomí, INI/CEMCA 1987, books.openedition.org/cemca/2714, paras 51-53.]

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: OpenEdition record books.openedition.org/cemca/3688 (Galinier 1979, N'yuhu, Introduction) exists; Google Books feed also returns the 1979 MAEFM print (id YrNVAAAAMAAJ) with the same transcription passage. A's copies we hold is not yet in the mirror (held_mirror/source_audit_2026-09-16/texc1235/ is empty) but A's own extract is on at work_2026-09-20/disc/texc1235/62,406 chars); the passage is at OpenEdition paras 63-70 exactly as quoted except that A's '[..]' elides paras 67-69 (the San Miguel ta mpa / tu mpa variant, which A reports under exceptions) and drops the footnote call '55' after 'Ecker'. Spanish 1987 edition extract paras 51-53 matches A's Spanish locator ('Es el otomi una lengua…
new_statements.relation_note: Consonant and vowel inventory for the zone, intervocalic voicing in Sierra parlers, glottal stop contrast, then the tone paragraph quoted; no tone count, no stress rule.
new_statements.rule_in_words: South-Huasteca (eastern) Otomi has tone contrasts (low vs high illustrated on the TAM proclitic tà/tá); 'accentuation' said to matter but no stress placement given; intonation contours differ between sub-dialects.
new_statements.exceptions: In some parlers (San Miguel zone) the tà/tá tonal contrast is replaced by a vowel difference (tà mpa vs tú mpa).
new_statements.identity_note: Ethnography of the 'Otomis du Sud de la Huasteca' (eastern Otomi of Hidalgo/Puebla/Veracruz), treated by the author as 'un seul et même dialecte'; his zone explicitly includes the 'région otomi de Texcatepec' (Texcatepec, Zontecomatlán, Ayotuxtla; para 9: its dialect is lexically the most divergent of the group), but phonological examples come from Santa Ana Hueytlalpan, San Lorenzo Achiotepec, San Miguel (otm, east2556) and the tone remark is not localised. Cluster-level statement spanning otm + otx; not a linguist's analysis.

sources.citation: Echegoyen Gleason, Artemisa (with K. Voigtlander). 1979. Luces contemporáneas del otomí: gramática del otomí de la sierra. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
sources.note: Sierra Otomi of San Antonio el Grande/San Gregorio (Huehuetla, Hidalgo; otm, east2556), not Texcatepec: p.23 'La sílaba con la acentuación principal es siempre la primera sílaba del radical', alternating rhythmic accent every other syllable. Intro (leaf ~147/200) lists 'otomí de Texcatepec (Veracruz)' as a separate variant of the eastern region; Garrido Cruz 2008:41 reports Echegoyen & Voigtlander p.c. that Texcatepec 'se debe de considerar como un dialecto aparte'.
